subject: Console rollout risk review: switch cost breakdown to Cost Model API (feature flag + rollback)
body:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 4:12 PM
Subject: Console rollout risk review: switch cost breakdown to Cost Model API (feature flag + rollback)

Laura / Aditya,

We’re planning to start the staged rollout of Console cost breakdown pages to the new Cost Model API this week (behind a flag). Before we flip anything in prod, I want a quick risk review + explicit go/no-go from Finance + Optimize on the plan.

Scope (v1):
- Console “Cost breakdown” views will call Cost Model API for per-request breakdown + aggregated breakdowns.
- No customer-facing pricing changes; this is internal attribution + UI consistency.

Rollout plan (proposed):
1) Ship code with feature flag OFF in prod (already in PR-28470).
2) Enable for internal tenants only (Redwood dogfood + a small set of beta orgs).
3) Ramp by % of orgs over ~5 business days.
4) Keep legacy estimator path intact for fast rollback.

Safety controls:
- Feature flag: console_cost_breakdown_use_cost_model_api
- Hard fallback: if API returns non-2xx or times out, Console falls back to legacy cost computation + shows “estimated” badge.
- Timeout: 250ms client-side budget; no retries on request path (we’ll rely on server-side caching). 

Observability gates (need agreement on what “healthy” means):
- p95 latency for the Console endpoints should not regress > 50ms.
- Cost Model API p95 < 150ms during business hours.
- Error rate < 0.5% (5xx + timeouts) sustained.
- Drift SLI within agreed band for 48h after enabling first cohort.

Questions I need answered in this thread:
1) Laura: are you comfortable with the UI showing the new breakdown taxonomy, given overhead allocation? Any constraints on the wording/labels to avoid confusion with invoices? (Ref: SUP-31844)
2) Aditya: any objections to Console depending on the same primitives Optimize uses? Any needed contract guarantees before we ramp? (Ref: SUP-31877 context, but we’re not enabling what-if in Console)

If you’re both OK, I’ll proceed with the internal-only enable tomorrow and schedule the % ramp pending the gates above.

Thanks,
Marissa

—
Marissa Cole
Console Product Owner
Redwood Inference



From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 5:01 PM
Subject: Re: Console rollout risk review: switch cost breakdown to Cost Model API (feature flag + rollback)

Thanks, Marissa.

I’m supportive, with two caveats so we don’t repeat the SUP-31844 pattern (Console ≠ invoice totals):

1) Labels / disclaimers
- Please avoid “Total cost” language if the totals can diverge from invoiced amounts due to timing windows, credits, or non-attributable overhead.
- “Estimated request-attributed compute cost” is fine.
- If you must show overhead, it needs to be explicitly “allocated overhead (policy)” and not implied as metered per-request.

2) Rollout gate: reconciliation window
- I’d like a 48–72h window where we compare “new breakdown sum” vs the current internal unit-economics report for the same tenant cohort.
- We don’t need perfect equality, but we need explained deltas. If we see material swings, we pause.

Question: in your fallback mode, will the UI still show the new taxonomy buckets or revert to the legacy breakdown? I’d prefer the UI not mix bucket semantics within the same time window.

Laura

—
Laura Bennett
Finance / FP&A
Redwood Inference



From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 5:24 PM
Subject: Re: Console rollout risk review: switch cost breakdown to Cost Model API (feature flag + rollback)

+1 to proceeding with the shared primitives.

Optimize-specific notes:
- We are aligned on using the canonical breakdown taxonomy and Cost Model API outputs as the source of truth for “request-attributed cost” and “allocated overhead.”
- Console should NOT call what-if endpoints on the hot path (sounds like you’re not).

Two concerns:
1) Request volume / caching
Console pages can generate a lot of repeated queries (filters, time range changes, etc.). Please confirm there’s aggressive caching/memoization in the Console backend so we don’t accidentally turn a dashboard view into a cost-model QPS spike. SUP-31905 mentioned endpoint latency affecting Console already.

2) Unknown fields / versioning
If the API adds new buckets or renames fields, I want Console to ignore unknown fields and not break rendering. (We’re taking that approach in Optimize.)

If you can confirm caching + versioning behavior, I’m a go for internal cohort.

Aditya

—
Aditya Rao
Optimize Product Owner
Redwood Inference



From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 6:03 PM
Subject: Re: Console rollout risk review: switch cost breakdown to Cost Model API (feature flag + rollback)

This is helpful — thank you both. Replies inline.

Laura:
> Please avoid “Total cost” language …
Agreed. We’ll use:
- “Request-attributed compute (estimate)”
- “Allocated overhead (policy)”
And we’ll add a short tooltip: “May differ from invoices due to credits, timing windows, and allocation policies.”

> fallback mode taxonomy
In fallback, we will revert to the legacy breakdown AND render the legacy buckets. We’ll also surface a banner: “Showing legacy estimates due to degraded cost model service.” The goal is to avoid mixing semantics.

> 48–72h reconciliation gate
OK. We’ll do dogfood + 2 beta orgs first, and run the compare daily. If unexplained deltas show up, we pause ramp. I’ll ask the team to drop a short daily note in #finance once we enable.

Aditya:
> request volume / caching
We’re adding a Console-side cache keyed by (tenant, model, time range, filters) with a 60s TTL. Also:
- Console backend batches UI queries into a single aggregated breakdown call per page view where possible.
- The API requests are bounded (no unbounded cardinality dimensions); if the UI asks for too many groups, we’ll show “Top N + other.”
- We’re limiting internal cohort to keep QPS predictable.

> unknown fields / versioning
Console client will be forward-compatible: ignore unknown fields; only render known buckets; any missing required bucket shows as “0” with a “data unavailable” indicator.

Rollback plan (explicit):
1) Flip feature flag OFF (immediate).
2) If still unstable, remove cohort allowlist (if used) + keep flag OFF.
3) If we hit severe p95 regression, we revert the deploy in the Console backend release train (separate from the cost-model service).

If you’re OK with the above, I’ll send Connor a note that we’re cleared to enable internal cohort tomorrow morning.

Marissa



From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 11, 2026 at 8:37 AM
Subject: Re: Console rollout risk review: switch cost breakdown to Cost Model API (feature flag + rollback)

Approved for internal cohort with the gating you described.

Two small adds:
- Please pin the reporting window in the UI (e.g., “data current as of …”) if telemetry lag is a common root cause. It helps support explain discrepancies.
- For the daily compare, can you include a note whether the delta is due to overhead allocation vs request-attributed compute? That’s the biggest confusion point.

Thanks for looping us in early.

Laura



From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 11, 2026 at 9:03 AM
Subject: Re: Console rollout risk review: switch cost breakdown to Cost Model API (feature flag + rollback)

Done — we’ll add “data current as of” to the header for the cost breakdown pages and include lag notes when applicable.

I’ll send Connor the go-ahead for internal cohort enable today, and we’ll start the daily delta note with the split you requested (request-attributed vs allocated overhead).

Marissa
